original.name: Propene
original.note: A radical chain: Br· adds first, to CH₂, giving the more stable secondary radical; the H comes last.

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: 2-Methylbutane
original.note: Bromination is very selective: the tertiary radical forms fastest.

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Propylbenzene
original.note: The benzylic radical is stabilised by the ring.

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: 4-Methylquinoline (lepidine)
original.ask: Where does the t-Bu radical attack?
original.note: A Minisci reaction: acid protonates the quinoline, which leaves C2 and C4 electron-poor, and the nucleophilic t-Bu radical (from pivalic acid) attacks there. C4 already carries the methyl.

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: 2-Methylquinoline (quinaldine)
original.ask: Where does the t-Bu radical attack?
original.note: With C2 blocked, the nucleophilic radical takes the other electron-poor position of the quinolinium ion, C4.

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: N-Methylpyrrole
original.note: •CF₃ is an electrophilic radical, so it behaves like an electrophile: it attacks the electron-rich C2 of the pyrrole.

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Methyl acrylate
original.ask: Where does the cyclohexyl radical add?
original.note: Giese addition: the nucleophilic radical adds to the unhindered β-carbon, where the LUMO is largest, and leaves a radical stabilised by the ester.

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Tetrahydrofuran
original.note: Polarity matching in hydrogen-atom transfer: the electrophilic Cl• abstracts the hydridic C–H next to oxygen, and the nucleophilic α-oxy radical it leaves is then coupled by nickel.

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Cyclopentanone
original.note: The α-C–H bonds next to the carbonyl are electron-poor, so the electrophilic excited decatungstate avoids them and abstracts a β-hydrogen, although the α radical would be the more stable one.

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: tert-Butyl radical
original.note: Three alkyl groups donate into the singly occupied orbital (SOMO) by hyperconjugation and raise it: tertiary alkyl radicals are strongly nucleophilic and add fast to acrylates (Giese reaction). The bulk does not slow them as it would an anion, because the transition state is early, with a long forming bond (2.55 Å for t-Bu• adding to methyl vinyl ketone).
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Isopropyl radical
original.note: Secondary alkyl radicals are nucleophilic: two alkyl groups raise the SOMO. Ethyl and isopropyl radicals made from ethane and propane add to Michael acceptors.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Methyl radical
original.note: Ambiphilic: the high-energy methyl radical barely discriminates between electron-rich and electron-poor alkenes. Under mild conditions it reacts as a nucleophile, adding to Michael acceptors and to azodicarboxylates.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Cyanomethyl radical
original.note: One electron-withdrawing group is enough to make a primary radical electrophilic: the nitrile's π* accepts density from the SOMO and lowers it. Cyanoalkyl radicals add to electron-rich enamines.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: (Ethoxycarbonyl)methyl radical
original.note: A primary radical with one ester is electrophilic: α-carbonyl radicals add to enamines and enol ethers.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: 2-(Methoxycarbonyl)prop-2-yl radical
original.note: A tertiary radical with a single ester is still nucleophilic: it is the growing chain end when methyl methacrylate polymerises, adding to the electron-poor monomer. Secondary and tertiary radicals need two electron-withdrawing groups to turn electrophilic.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Diethyl malonyl radical
original.note: Two esters lower the SOMO enough to make even a secondary radical electrophilic: malonyl radicals add to indoles and other electron-rich arenes.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Hydroxymethyl radical
original.note: The oxygen lone pair donates into the SOMO (n → p) and raises it: α-oxy radicals are strongly nucleophilic, even though oxygen is electronegative.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Tetrahydrofuran-2-yl radical
original.note: An α-oxy radical, among the most nucleophilic radicals known. Cl• or decatungstate hydrogen-atom transfer makes it from THF, and it adds to electron-poor alkenes or to nickel.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: N-Boc-pyrrolidin-2-yl radical
original.note: Nitrogen is less electronegative than oxygen, so α-amino radicals are even more nucleophilic, and they stay so with a Boc group on nitrogen. They add to protonated heteroarenes (Minisci reactions) and are captured by nickel.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: (Methylthio)methyl radical
original.note: α-Sulfur radicals, like α-F, α-Cl, α-Br and α-I radicals, are moderately nucleophilic: the lone pair donates by π overlap. Made by metal-hydride HAT from vinyl sulfides, they add to acrylamides.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: (Trimethylsilyl)methyl radical
original.note: A primary α-silyl radical is electrophilic: the SOMO gives density to silicon's low-lying acceptor orbitals, which lowers it. With two more alkyl groups (a tertiary α-silyl radical) it is nucleophilic again.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: 2-(Dimethylphenylsilyl)prop-2-yl radical
original.note: A tertiary α-silyl radical is nucleophilic: it adds to methyl acrylate (Giese). The two alkyl groups outweigh silicon's acceptor effect, which wins only in primary and secondary α-silyl radicals.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Trifluoromethyl radical
original.note: Mostly electrophilic: three electronegative fluorines outweigh their π donation, and •CF₃ adds to electron-rich arenes and alkenes. It is ambiphilic, though, and also adds to some electron-poor heteroarenes and alkenes.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Difluoromethyl radical
original.note: Unlike •CF₃, •CF₂H reacts as a nucleophile with heteroarenes: it attacks protonated, electron-poor positions as alkyl radicals do in Minisci reactions.

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Phenyl radical
original.note: A σ radical: the SOMO is an sp² orbital in the ring plane, at right angles to the π system, so ring substituents barely change it. Its s character makes it electrophilic, and its high energy makes it ambiphilic: aryl radicals add to electron-rich and electron-poor arenes alike.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: 2-Methylprop-1-enyl radical
original.note: Vinyl radicals are σ radicals with more s character than alkyl radicals: they are electrophilic and usually add to electron-rich or plain alkenes, which is why vinyl radical cyclisations onto unactivated alkenes work.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Phenylethynyl radical
original.note: Alkynyl radicals have the most s character of all and are electrophilic: in a competition, phenylethynyl radicals attack the more electron-rich of two arenes.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Acetyl radical
original.note: The oxygen lone pair is held in line with the SOMO, so acyl radicals are exceptionally nucleophilic: an umpolung of the electrophilic carbonyl carbon. They add to acrylonitriles and vinyl sulfones, giving ketones.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: tert-Butoxyl radical
original.note: Oxygen is far more electronegative than carbon (3.44 against 2.55), so oxyl radicals are strongly electrophilic. They seldom add to π bonds; they abstract hydridic H atoms (HAT) or fragment (β-scission).
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Piperidin-1-yl (aminyl) radical
original.note: N is more electronegative than C (3.04): aminyl radicals are electrophilic and aminate electron-rich arenes. Protonated, as aminium radical cations, they are more electrophilic still.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Piperidinium radical cation
original.note: Aminium radical cations are among the most electrophilic radicals: they add to electron-rich arenes and abstract hydridic C–H bonds next to O and N.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: N-Methylacetamidyl radical
original.note: Amidyl radicals are electrophilic N radicals: they add to electron-rich π systems and abstract δ-C–H bonds (1,5-HAT), as in Hofmann–Löffler-type remote functionalisation.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Butanethiyl radical
original.note: Sulfur is barely more electronegative than carbon (2.58 against 2.55), yet thiyl radicals are electrophilic: the thiol–ene reaction is fastest with electron-rich alkenes such as vinyl ethers and norbornene.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Bromine atom
original.note: Halogen atoms are strongly electrophilic: Br• adds to electron-rich alkenes (radical HBr addition) and picks out hydridic C–H bonds.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Chlorine atom
original.note: Cl• is one of the most electrophilic radicals: it abstracts the hydridic C–H next to the oxygen of THF, and nickel then couples the α-oxy radical.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Tris(trimethylsilyl)silyl radical
original.note: Silicon is less electronegative than carbon, so silyl radicals are nucleophilic: (TMS)₃Si• adds to methyl acrylate but not to 1-hexene or styrene, and abstracts halogen atoms fast.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: NHC–boryl radical
original.note: Boron is less electronegative than carbon (2.04): ligated boryl radicals are nucleophilic. An NHC–BH₂• radical added to methyl acrylate at least 380 times faster than to ethyl vinyl ether.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Diethoxyphosphoryl radical
original.note: Phosphonyl radicals, which carry a P=O, are electrophilic: they add to unactivated alkenes and enol ethers, although phosphorus is less electronegative than carbon.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: NHC–boryl radical
original.note: At least 380 times faster to the acrylate: a nucleophilic radical wants an electron-poor partner.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: tert-Butyl radical
original.note: The nucleophilic t-Bu• radical adds to the electron-poor alkene (a Giese addition); the electron-rich enol ether is a poor match.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Diethyl malonyl radical
original.note: Two esters make the malonyl radical electrophilic, so it adds to the electron-rich enol ether.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Tetrahydrofuran-2-yl radical
original.note: The α-oxy radical is strongly nucleophilic and adds to the acrylate; 1-hexene offers no polar help.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Butanethiyl radical
original.note: Thiyl radicals are electrophilic: in thiol–ene chemistry vinyl ethers react far faster than acrylates, which tend to polymerise instead.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Trifluoromethyl radical
original.note: •CF₃ is electrophilic and attacks the electron-rich pyrrole, at C2, like an electrophile would.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Acetyl radical
original.note: Acyl radicals are nucleophilic and add to electron-poor alkenes, giving ketones.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Tris(trimethylsilyl)silyl radical
original.note: The nucleophilic silyl radical adds to methyl acrylate; with 1-hexene or styrene no reaction was seen.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Piperidinium radical cation
original.note: The electrophilic aminium radical cation aminates electron-rich arenes such as anisole.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Cyanomethyl radical
original.note: One nitrile makes the primary radical electrophilic, so it prefers the electron-rich enol ether.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: Bromine atom
original.note: Br• is electrophilic and adds to the electron-richer alkene.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021

molecule_asset_reference: original.mol index points to molecular drawings in upstream HTML

original.name: N-Boc-pyrrolidin-2-yl radical
original.note: The nucleophilic α-amino radical adds to the protonated, electron-poor heteroarene: a Minisci reaction.
src: Parsaee et al., Nat. Rev. Chem. 2021
